title: zTunnel error io error: invalid peer certificate: Other(OtherError(identity verification error: peer did not present the expected SAN
body:
### Is this the right place to submit this?

- [x] This is not a security vulnerability or a crashing bug
- [x] This is not a question about how to use Istio

### Bug Description

I'm running a multi primary, multi cluster ambient mesh setup with zTunnel east west gateways between my clusters `cluster1` and `cluster2`.
I installed Istio using these instructions: https://istio.io/latest/docs/setup/install/multicluster/multi-primary_multi-network/
and used Helm with the following shared values:
```
istiod:
  env:
    AMBIENT_ENABLE_MULTI_NETWORK: "true"
  profile: ambient
  meshConfig:
    defaultConfig:
      proxyMetadata:
        ISTIO_META_DNS_CAPTURE: "true"
        ISTIO_META_DNS_AUTO_ALLOCATE: "true"
cni:
  profile: ambient
ztunnel:
  profile: ambient
```
and for cluster specific values:
`cluster1`:
```
istiod:
  global:
    meshID: mesh1
    multiCluster:
      clusterName: cluster1
    network: network1

ztunnel:
  global:
    network: network1
  multiCluster:
    clusterName: cluster1
```
`cluster2`
```
istiod:
  global:
    meshID: mesh1
    multiCluster:
      clusterName: cluster2
    network: network2

ztunnel:
  global:
    network: network2
  multiCluster:
    clusterName: cluster2
```

My clusters are using intermediate certs from the same root CA. (Followed the instructions here: https://istio.io/latest/docs/tasks/security/cert-management/plugin-ca-cert/)
The clusters exist on different networks and in different regions (AWS)
Output from `istioctl remote-clusters`
```
istioctl remote-clusters --context=cluster1
NAME                   SECRET                                          STATUS     ISTIOD
cluster1                                                               synced     istiod-75d587bb9d-drgx4
cluster2               istio-system/istio-remote-secret-cluster1       synced     istiod-75d587bb9d-drgx4
```
```
NAME                   SECRET                                                  STATUS     ISTIOD
cluster2                                                                       synced     istiod-8567699f9f-hd7ms
cluster1               istio-system/istio-remote-secret-cluster2               synced     istiod-8567699f9f-hd7ms
```
I have a global service called `my-service` that looks similar to this that is deployed in `cluster1` and `cluster2`:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: my-service
    istio.io/global: "true"
  name: my-service
  namespace: namespace1 (and another one in namespace2)
spec:
  clusterIP: x.x.x.x
  clusterIPs:
  - x.x.x.x
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ports:
  - port: 3000
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 3000
  selector:
    app: my-service
  type: ClusterIP
```
Both `namespace1` and `namespace2` in both clusters have been labeled `istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient`
Within `cluster1`, I have the `Deployment` that this service points to scaled down to 0 replicas so that any queries to `my-service` would be routed to `cluster2`.
For the _majority_ of requests, this works properly:
From a `Pod` in `cluster1`:
```
curl my-service.namespace1:3000
SUCCESS
```
with the following log in zTunnel:
```
ztunnel-9bnrk 2025-12-22T17:34:19.554393Z    info    access    connection complete    src.addr=10.100.154.220:55714 src.workload="curl-5c79bf695-jl5pb" src.namespace="namespace1" src.identity="spiffe://cluster.local/ns/namespace1/sa/default" dst.addr=x.x.x.x:15008 dst.hbone_addr=<redacted-host>:3000 dst.service="<redacted-host>" dst.workload="NetworkGateway/region-1/x.x.x.x/0" dst.namespace="istio
-system" dst.identity="spiffe://cluster.local/ns/istio-system/sa/istio-eastwestgateway" direction="outbound" bytes_sent=114 bytes_recv=250 duration="14ms"
```
However, occasionally I'll get a failure with a zTunnel log like this:
```
ztunnel-9bnrk 2025-12-22T16:42:07.046871Z    error    access    connection complete    src.addr=10.100.154.220:52658 src.workload="curl-5c79bf695-jl5pb"
src.namespace="namespace1" src.identity="spiffe://cluster.local/ns/namespace1/sa/default" dst.addr=x.x.x.x:15008 dst.hbone_addr=<redacted-host>:3000 dst.service="<redacted-host>" dst.workload="NetworkGateway/region-2/x.x.x.x/0" dst.namespace="istio-system" dst.identity="spiffe://cluster.local/ns/istio-system/sa/istio-eastwestgateway" direction="outbound" bytes_sent=0 bytes_recv=0 duration="187
ms" error="io error: invalid peer certificate: Other(OtherError(identity verification error: peer did not present the expected SAN (spiffe://cluster.local/ns/namespace1/sa/default), got spiffe://cluster.local/ns/namespace2/sa/default))"
```
Notice how the destination namespace is `namespace1`, but for some reason `cluster2` occasionally presents a cert for `namespace2`. 
The desired behavior is that when I query my global service `my-service` on `namespace1` that `cluster2` would present the expected SAN of `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/namespace1/sa/default` instead of the incorrect SAN of `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/namespace2/sa/default`.
Any ideas on what's going on here?


### Version

```Text
`cluster1`

istioctl version --context=cluster1
client version: 1.28.1
control plane version: 1.28.1
data plane version: 1.28.1 (4 proxies)


`cluster2`

istioctl version --context=cluster2                                                                                                                                                                                   
client version: 1.28.1
control plane version: 1.28.1
data plane version: 1.28.1 (14 proxies)



kubectl version
Client Version: v1.34.3
Kustomize Version: v5.7.1
Server Version: v1.32.9



helm version --short
v3.19.3+g0707f56
```

### Additional Information

_No response_


comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@reporter just to make sure I understand you, you're saying that your have service `my-service` in namespace `namespace1` and a service with the same name in `namespace2` in both clusters, is that correct?

The error you've presented seems to suggest the following:

1. ztunnel tried to route a request to service `my-service` in `namespace1` to a remote cluster (that's why `dst.workload` points to a network gateway)
2. E/W gateway presented an expected identity and the error does not complain about E/W gateway identity, so I conclude that E/W gateway terminated the outer HBONE tunnel correctly
3. For whatever reason, E/W gateway seem to be routing the request to the `my-service` service in `namespace2` instead of the one in `namespace1` in the remote cluster

Can you share the E/W gateway envoy config in the remote cluster? You can get it with the command `istioctl pc all <E/W gateway pod name> -n istio-system -o yaml`?

I will try to reproduce it locally in the meantime, I'd imagine if we confusing the services between namespace it shouldn't be that hard.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @reporter one more thing, I see in the config that you named networks `network1` and `network2`, but in the logs network gateways are using `region-1` and `region-2`, was it a copying mistake when your reported the bug and in the actual setup there is no difference?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I created a similar setup locally and checked EDS configuration on E/W gateway and it appear to be fine - we are not mixing up endpoints from different namespaces. And I wasn't able to reproduce the issue yet.

@reporter said that the issue happens after some time, so I will let it bake for a few hours and see if I'm going to notice anything.

Also answering some of the questions posted above:

> Does it matter that both of these services share the same gateway ip?

No it does not matter and it's expected that you'll have a gateway per cluster and therefore a single IP. When ztunnel (or waypoint) talks to remote network, it uses HBONE protocol, which is essnetially HTTP2 connect, as part of that connect request we can transfer all the information that E/W gateway needs to route the request correctly. You can see in the logs for example `dst.hbone_addr` field which include the fully qualified service name and port - that's what E/W gateway will receive.

I'm basing my suggestion on the fact that ztunnel tries to reach E/W gateway (you can see it from the logs), it does not complain about E/W gateway identity, but it does complain about end workload identity, so it means that it reached E/W gateway, E/W gateway routed the request to some workload and that workload responded with some identity, but it was not the identity that ztunnel expected. 

I don't know what the issue is, but I'd like to make sure that E/W gateway routing configuration is in order. I also consider the fact that out of all ambient components ambient E/W gateway is the yongest, so if I wanted to search for a bug that's where I'd consdier starting first.

Can you please provide clarifications regarding this:

> @reporter just to make sure I understand you, you're saying that your have service my-service in namespace namespace1 and a service with the same name in namespace2 in both clusters, is that correct?

In either of your setup, when you test service X and encounter this error, does this service exist in the same namespace in both clusters?

> Could this potentially be a caching issue where maybe the identity of spiffe://cluster.local/ns/namespace2/sa/service-account-2 got cached and then starting serving it when requests for my-service-1 started coming in?

ztunnel is deployed per node, so one ztunnel serves multiple workloads at the same time - it's normal for ztunnels even in single cluster deployment.

Purely hypotehtically there could be some caching issue somewhere in ztunnel, but given that ztunnels are designed to handle multiple workloads with different identities at the same time and given that fact that we haven't seen the issue you're describing in single cluster ambient deployment where such caching also could happen, I think that ztunnel is less likely to be the cause here compared to E/W gateway.

And again, I don't know what the issue here yet, but we need to start ruling out possibilities to get to the bottom of it and I'd like to start with E/W gateway first.

> Running istioctl pc all <E/W gateway pod name> -n istio-system -o yaml gives me about 6400 lines of config, and it looks like there's some sensitive info inside of it. Is there a particular part of the config you want me to share?

comments.body:
I think I know what the issue is - I suspect that the issue is in envoy. When we use `envoy.string` factory for the filter state it's not correctly shared with the upstream connections. And it looks like somebody actually beat me to it and added a fix to upstream envoy.

I'm going to test it out now...

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
The test passed - the fix seem to have worked. I need to think a bit about a better fix and why we didn't hit the same problem before, but here is seem to be the gist of the problem:

1. Istio configuration for Envoy consists of multiple layers of listeners, specifically for E/W gateway in ambient, we have two listeners that are relevant: `connect_terminate` and `main_internal`.
2. When we send request over E/W gateway we wrap it in double-HBONE tunnel, E/W gateway terminates the outer HBONE tunnel, but transfers the inner HBONE tunnel to the destination unmodified
    - E/W gateway figures out the destination by looking at the authority and headers of the outer-HBONE CONNECT request
3. `connect_terminate` listener is responsible for terminating the outer HBONE tunnel and extracting and saving all the required details for later use, but the actual routing (e.g., picking the right endpoint) happens in the `main_internal` listener
    - we use Envoy filter state to communicate the required details from `connect_terminate` listener to `main_internal` listener

The important part here is that we use `envoy.string` encoded filter state values for communication between `connect_terminate` and `main_internal` listeners. `envoy.string` filter state, as it turns out, does not affect connection pooling because it does not implement `Hashable` interface. Which basically means that it's possible that two requests with completely different authority will use the same connection pool.

I'm not super familiar with the Envoy code after that point, but checking quickly, it appears that using the same connection pool implies using the same transport socket options which is where we preserve the filter state objects to be shared with the upstream internal listener.

We can deal with that issue, but what surprises me is that we rely on `envoy.string` filter state objects (or specifically `connect_authority` `set_filter_state` filter) is used in waypoints and not just E/W gateways. So how come we don't see the same issue in plain waypoint traffic?

I think the answer here lies in the difference in authority between inter and intra network requests. Within the same network we use IP address and port as authority in the HBONE CONNECT request. For multi-network, we cannot rely on VIPs, so we have to use hostname and port.

Now, why is that important? We store authority to multiple different filter state objects used for different purposes, in particular we also try to save it to `envoy.filters.listener.original_dst.local_ip`. It works differently from `envoy.string` in the sense that it implements `Hashable` interface. The problem is that this filter state object can only accept valid IP + port and fails to accept the hostname.

@participant1 @participant2 @participant1 - I think you might be interested in this one. That might be relevant to moving ambient HBONE to using hostnames instead of VIPs for authority as it might not work as intended in Envoy. It's not a big deal and it could be fixed, but requires a bit of work before we can move ztunnel to using hostnames instead of VIPs as request the authority.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I think we are lucky and don't need that fix at the moment.

There is an option in Envoy to allocate a separate connection pool per downstream connection, so if we assume that ztunnel (or waypoint) does not multiplex requests to different services over the same connection to the E/W gateway (which I think we don't do), it should be enough to just require E/W gateway to create a separate connection pool per dowstream connection and it will fix the problem.

I think we still should migrate to `envoy.hashable_string` instead of `envoy.string` as a less fragile approach, but we don't have to cherry pick the fix to envoy 1.37 just to fix this ticket - the next Istio release will pick up `envoy.hashable_string` and we can start using it in newer Istio releases.

As for why we don't see it that much, it looks like the other factor is the client address. Basically different client addresses result in using different connection pools, but when requests arrive to E/W gateway from the same IP we can hit this issue. So basically the same pod has to connect to different services through the E/W gateway in somewhat close succession and don't do any retries to overcome transient issues.

Still, it's a bit weird that we didn't hit it in our tests before, I need to play around with the integration tests a bit to see why we didn't catch it and fix that.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Another factor to consider here is the number of threads Envoy uses - Envoy has a separate connection pool per working thread, so running with many worker threads makes hitting this issue less likely as well.
